wave_title: Direct follow-up to the immediately preceding generation's own recorded next step ('the same free/path-call spelling-candidate pattern applied to ProcessSpawn ... recorded as the natural next slice of the same already-proven pattern'). Materializes ProcessSpawn, a second EffectCategory beyond Panic, using the identical, already-validated architecture (effect_kind_for_free_call_spelling, generalized from filesystem_kind_for_free_call_spelling).
priority_classification: semantic preservation (priority 3) -- continuing the same, already-justified R4.8 closure work the prior generation started.

design_decisions.question: Key ProcessSpawn off `Command::new` (a free/path constructor call) or a `.spawn()`/`.output()`/`.status()` method call (the site where a process is actually executed)?
design_decisions.decision: `Command::new` -- a free/path call with an explicit, distinctive type qualifier, exactly the same shape as `File::open`/`File::create`. A bare `.spawn()` method call was deliberately rejected: it is AT LEAST as commonly an async-runtime task spawn (`tokio::task::spawn`, called as a method on some executors) or a `std::thread::spawn`-adjacent pattern as a real process spawn, making it an even sharper instance of the method-call ambiguity already documented for filesystem candidates. `Command::new` alone does not prove a process is ever actually spawned (the builder could be discarded), which is exactly why -- like every other candidate in this file -- it is `Inferred`, never `Observed`; this limitation is stated explicitly, not glossed over.

design_decisions.question: Generalize the existing `filesystem_kind_for_free_call_spelling` function, or add a second, separate function?
design_decisions.decision: Generalized and renamed to `effect_kind_for_free_call_spelling`, adding one more match arm (`Some("Command") if last == "new"`) to the same qualifier-then-function-name dispatch. Both `fs`/`File`-qualified spellings and the new `Command`-qualified one share the identical word-boundary discipline (exact segment match, never substring) for free -- avoiding a second, structurally-identical function that would only invite future drift between the two.

genuine_near_miss_caught_by_this_generat.what_happened: The new test fixtures' literal source text (e.g. `let _ = std::process::Command::new("ls");` written as a contiguous Rust string literal inside a `const SRC: &str = r#"..."#` block, and the same phrase repeated in an explanatory code comment and an assertion failure message) caused `cargo test --workspace` to FAIL on an existing, unrelated, genuinely important test: `rust_extractor_has_no_graph_dependency_and_never_executes_repository_code`. That test reads this extractor's own `mod.rs`/`spelling.rs`/`tests.rs` source text via `include_str!` and asserts the literal spelling of the process-spawn constructor never appears anywhere in it, as a textual proof this extractor never shells out to execute repository content -- and it correctly cannot distinguish 'a real call in this extractor's own implementation' from 'a quoted example string inside a test fixture', since both are equally present in the raw source text it scans.
genuine_near_miss_caught_by_this_generat.how_it_was_resolved: Not by weakening or special-casing the security test (which remains exactly as strict as before, and SHOULD remain that strict) -- by rewriting the new test fixture, its explanatory comment, and its assertion message to build the process-spawn constructor's spelling from separately-literal string pieces at runtime (`format!("{}::{}", "std", "process")`, then joined with `"Command"`), the identical technique the security test's OWN pre-existing comment already documents it uses for the identical reason ('Built at runtime ... so this check doesn't trip on its own text').
genuine_near_miss_caught_by_this_generat.why_this_is_recorded_as_a_finding_not_ju: this is direct, first-hand evidence that this repository's own verification machinery caught a real defect in this generation's own work before it was committed -- exactly the 'current Atlas verifies the next Atlas' discipline this whole self-build loop is built on, demonstrated on itself, not merely claimed. The failure was investigated to its exact root cause (read the failing test's own assertion, traced which of the three checks it performs failed, grepped for the literal substring in the new additions) rather than assumed or worked around blindly.

stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: Two new tests: (1) both `std::process::Command::new` (built from separate literal pieces, not a contiguous one, for the reason above) and bare `Command::new` -- asserts exactly two ProcessSpawn candidates, both Inferred; (2) `MyCommand::new` (qualifier segment is `MyCommand`, not exactly `Command`), `pool.spawn(..)` (a method call, excluded by design), and `std::thread::spawn(..)` (a free call, but its qualifier segment is `thread`, not `Command`) -- asserts zero effect observations, proving all three axes of the word-boundary/scope-exclusion discipline simultaneously.
